title: A row of the event log (events_<side>_<boot>_<n>.jsonl)
description: One thing that happened on one side of the game, written by the bridge mod (Shared/EventLog.lua) and never changed. docs/contracts/bridge-protocol.md, "The event log". Its kind, knows, attention and payload fields are held to the registry (events/kinds) by the host's reader.

seq.description: 1, 2, 3 ... within one boot of the side's Lua state.

tick.description: The side's tick count (bridge ticks) when it was written.

t.description: The game process's monotonic milliseconds: one clock for both sides.

knows.description: Who could know it: player - perceived through the game itself (an open window, a prompt, the combat log); omniscient - state a player cannot see (Osiris internals, staging, the detailed families, a game-log row the party did not perceive). A host serving a fair client gives it player rows only.

class.description: The class of the verb that made the row, on a kind whose registry entry has classPerRow; absent: the kind's own class.

key.description: The waiting state an attention row opens or closes (window:trade, combat, film ...).

attention.description: begin: opens `key` and is news; hold: opens it quietly; end: closes it and is news; release: closes it quietly; news: told, waits for nothing.

side.description: Which side wrote the row: given by the host when it merges the two logs into one stream; absent in the files.

unplaced.description: Why the host could not place the row by the registry of the game that wrote it (nor by its own): a kind in neither, a knows or attention the kind does not declare. Given by the host; absent in the files. The row is kept; a fair stream takes it as omniscient.

scope.description: The stage scope open when the row was written: the seq of its scope_begin row.

payload.description: What the kind carries: the fields its registry entry names.
